appraisal_events.evidence: dit-elle à son mari pour diminuer un peu ma faute en ayant l'air de croire que j'avais obéi à une propension commune à tous et à laquelle il était difficile de résister
appraisal_events.explanation: The duchess publicly recasts the narrator's near-mention of Swann as a universal impulse rather than a personal fault, shielding him from blame in front of her husband.

status_effects.explanation: The duchess's tactful excuse-making keeps the narrator socially covered rather than singled out for an awkward misstep, a mild protective gesture.

ambiguities: The duchess's protective excuse for the narrator is staged with comic, fussy self-attention ('c'est épouvantable, heureusement que je me suis arrêtée à temps'), so it is uncertain whether the passage endorses her tact as genuinely gracious toward the narrator or lightly ironizes her performance of social delicacy; the effect on the narrator is read conservatively as mild and protective rather than a clear elevation.

Gilberte and Swann are both invoked only as the unspoken, protected topic (the taboo of mentioning her late father in front of her); neither receives a distinct local evaluative event of their own in this passage, so both are omitted as candidates.
